title: Kabsa
description: Kabsa is a traditional Arabic spiced rice dish made with tender chicken or lamb cooked in a rich blend of aromatic spices, tomatoes, and vegetables, served over fragrant basmati rice and garnished with nuts and herbs.

ingredients.title: For the Meat
items: 1.5 kg chicken (whole, cut into pieces) or lamb
1 tsp black lime powder (loomi) or 1 dried black lime
Salt and black pepper to taste

ingredients.title: For the Rice
items: 3 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked 30 minutes
4 ½ cups chicken stock or water

instruction.title: Instructions
steps:
1. Prepare the Meat:
• Heat oil/ghee in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
• Sauté onions until golden brown. Add garlic and stir for 1 minute.
• Add chicken or lamb pieces and sear until lightly browned.
• Add tomatoes, carrots, bell pepper, Kabsa spice mix, cinnamon, cardamom, loomi, cumin, cloves, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Cook 5–7 minutes until aromatic.

2. Cook the Rice:
• In a separate pot, heat ghee/oil and sauté whole spices (cinnamon stick, cloves, cardamom pods, bay leaf) for 1 minute.
• Add rice and tomato paste, stir to coat grains.
• Pour in chicken stock or water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15–20 minutes until rice is tender.

3. Combine Meat and Rice:
• Layer cooked rice over the meat in the pot (do not stir).
• Cover tightly and simmer on very low heat for 10–15 minutes to allow flavors to meld.

4. Finish and Serve:
• Transfer rice to a large serving platter.
• Place meat on top.
• Garnish with toasted almonds, pine nuts, fried onions, and parsley.
• Serve with yogurt or fresh salad.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve with yogurt or garlic sauce
Pair with Arabic salad or fattoush
Enjoy as a festive main dish for gatherings
Serve hot with lemon wedges for extra brightness

chefTips: Use ghee for a richer, more traditional aroma.
Lightly toast rice in ghee before boiling for deeper flavor.
Slow-cook meat to fully absorb spices.
Use basmati rice for fluffy, separate grains.
Adjust spice levels gradually—Kabsa should be aromatic, not overly spicy.
